title: fix(metadata-protocol)!: an uninstall that would drop a table another stored row still serves is refused 409 before anything is removed
body:
Fixes #23473

Clause-②: no

## What changes

`deletePackage` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`) now refuses the WHOLE uninstall `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` before its first durable step (step 4, the `sys_packages` delete) when, without `keepData: true`, an active object row of the package shares its object with another stored active row: another package's row, or the package-less row. Nothing is removed: the `sys_packages` row, the registry entry, every `sys_metadata` row, the tables and their records all stay. The refusal names each shared object and the rows that keep it, and prescribes the ways out.

Before this, the per-item delete met #23415's per-object `409` only after step 4, collected it in `failed[]` and the door answered `400 PACKAGE_DELETE_PARTIAL` over a package that was no longer installed while its row of the shared object stayed stored and served.

Shape B, per the lane decision on the card (`6168058499`). Not shape C (uninstall and quietly keep the shared table).

## Governing text

`deletePackage`'s own docblock at `1baf976cf9`, quoted:

> 3. the registry's uninstall refusal (another package extends an object this one owns, ADR-0029), asked through `SchemaRegistry.assertPackageUninstallable` — pure; thrown as is;

> [#21276] The steps, in order. Nothing durable happens before step 4, so a refusal at any of steps 1–4 leaves everything as it was:

A shared object is the same kind of stake as an extended one, so it joins step 3's up-front refusal. The docblock's step 3 now names both refusals; the numbering, and with it "nothing durable happens before step 4", is unchanged.

## How the condition is read (premise, measured)

- **Same reads as the per-item delete, no new store surface.** For each active object row whose table the uninstall would drop (`shouldDropStorage`, the same guard: object type, active, not `sys_`), the pre-flight calls `packagelessAddress(type, name, undefined, 'active')`, the private address read `deleteMetaItem` itself takes for that row (its `rowsAtAddress`), with the type folded as `deleteMetaItem` folds it (`canonicalMetaType`, then `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR`). It refuses exactly when that delete would: the package holds a row there and another package's row or the package-less row stays. A failed read is the uninstall's step-2 read failure (`metadataReadFailureError`), never "not shared".
- **`keepData: true` really skips every drop.** The only table-drop call sites are `deleteMetaItem`'s two paths into `dropObjectStorage`, both gated by `shouldDropStorage` on the request's `dropStorage`, and `deletePackage` sends `dropStorage` only when `keepData !== true`. So with `keepData` sharing decides nothing and the pre-flight reads nothing.
- **No measured flow needs shape C.** `deletePackage` has two callers: the `DELETE /api/v1/packages/:id` door, and `rollBackUnmanagedImport`, whose import refuses a name another row holds before it writes anything (`unmanagedImportCollisions`). The install-local uninstall door does not call it.

## Error code

The pre-flight answers `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` / `409`, which is also the code the per-item refusal (`dropStorageRemainingRowsRefusal`) answers for the same rows. Step 3's own refusal, an object extended by another package, used to be a code-less `Error` that the door answered `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`. Since PR #23522 (#23505, `989aa483fd`) it answers `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with the way out, pinned in `package-uninstall-store-refusal.integration.test.ts` on `main`. So both up-front uninstall refusals now share one code. No code is minted.

## The refusal, as measured (two shared objects)

```text
Uninstall package 'com.probe.p' with keepData (?keepData=true; keepData: true in process), which keeps all its object tables, or first delete, without dropStorage, its row or the other rows of each object below (DELETE /api/v1/meta/object/NAME?package=ID). Nothing was removed: an uninstall drops an object's table only with the object's last row, and 2 objects of this package are also held by other rows: 'probe_ticket' (its row bound to package 'com.probe.q' remains); 'probe_case' (its row bound to package 'com.probe.q' remains).
```

The second way out answers the card body's concern with shape B: deleting the package's own row of each shared object first (no `dropStorage`) keeps that table for the other rows, and the uninstall then still drops the tables the package alone held. That path is pinned too.

## Merge round after the queue ejection (run 38682506920)

The PR left the merge queue: `Test Core (6/6)` failed on queue commit `5e97584201` (`main` `8d05456cbe` plus this PR). `main` was merged in as a merge commit, `192d2051da` (no conflict; `protocol.ts` auto-merged). Reproduced on that commit, the three cases of the pin where P and Q both hold the object failed in setup, before any assertion:

```text
Error: Cannot layer object 'probe_ticket': the overlay is bound to package 'com.probe.q', but the object is owned by package 'com.probe.p'. An object has exactly one registry entry, ...
```

Cause: #23510 (`222293f60a`, ADR-0029 D9.9) landed on `main` after this PR's previous merge base `f9b421716d` (`merge-base --is-ancestor` exit 1, control leg `f9b421716d~60` exit 0; it is in `8d05456cbe`, exit 0). The save door now refuses a save into a second package of an object a runtime-authored row owns (`OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH` / `422`), so the pin's fixture could no longer save Q's row. `protocol.ts` was not the cause and is unchanged by this round; the step-3 CONTROL in `package-uninstall-store-refusal.integration.test.ts` (uninstalling the extending package) passes on the merged tree.

**Does the shared state still arise?** Measured on the merged tree, real `ObjectQL` over better-sqlite3, the real protocol and `HttpDispatcher.handlePackages` (one-time readings, probe not kept):

| producer | result | stored active rows |
|:--|:--|:--|
| save door: P, then Q | Q refused `422 OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH` | P |
| save door: P, then a save naming no package | addressed to P's row | P |
| save door: a save naming no package first, then P, then Q | all three succeed (the registry owner is the `sys_metadata` sentinel, which D9.9 leaves out) | P, Q, package-less |
| Q saves a DRAFT before P's row exists; P publishes; Q promotes (`publishMetaItem`, `package` Q) | promotion succeeds; the registry keeps P | P, Q |
| the same, promoted by `POST /api/v1/packages/com.probe.q/publish-drafts` at the door handler | `200`, `outcome: published`, `failed: []`; the registry keeps P | P, Q |
| `duplicatePackage` P to Q (`targetNamespace` given) | the copy is renamed `qq_probe_ticket` | P |
| boot (`loadMetaFromDb`) over a stored Q row beside P's | counts the row in `errors`, leaves it stored (code reading) | unchanged |

So the state still arises: through today's doors (the last two save-door rows), and as rows stored before D9.9, which stay at rest. On each door-reached state the uninstall of P without `keepData` answered `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` and removed nothing. The pre-flight guards a live path.

**The fixture fix.** `twoPackageObject` now saves P's row through the door, as before, and seeds Q's row straight into the store as a row stored before D9.9 (the save's shape, checksum by `hashSpec`), the way #23510 re-seeded its own two sibling fixtures. It does not use the draft-promotion path: that path is a D9.9 gap, and a fixture built on it would break again when the gap closes. Every case assertion is unchanged; the package-less case and the CONTROL are unchanged.

## Tests

The pin, `packages/runtime/src/package-uninstall-shared-object.integration.test.ts`, at the uninstall door itself: real `ObjectQL` over a real better-sqlite3 `SqlDriver` (real tables), the real `PackageServicePlugin` (`sys_packages`), the real protocol and the real `HttpDispatcher.handlePackages`. Five cases:

1. P and Q hold an object, uninstall P without `keepData`: `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` (status and code asserted), message names the object, Q and `keepData`; the `sys_packages` row, `GET /packages/P` 200, both rows, the table, the record and the registry entry all intact.
2. The same with the package-less row as the other holder.
3. `?keepData=true`: 200, `failed: []`, P gone, Q's row, the table and the record stay, the registry serves Q's definition.
4. P's own row deleted first (no `dropStorage`): the uninstall answers 200, `failed: []`, keeps the shared table and drops the table P alone held.
5. CONTROL: an object one package holds — 200, row gone, table dropped.

Readings at `addcca0cf5` (`--maxWorkers=2`, each under the shared verify lock, verdict from its `VERDICT command-exit` line):

- red before, at the merge commit `192d2051da`: the pin 3 failed / 2 passed (the setup error above); the two sibling uninstall integration files passed (11 tests).
- the pin: 5/5 passed.
- `@objectstack/runtime` uninstall sweep (every `src/package-uninstall-*.integration.test.ts`, every `src/domains/packages-*.test.ts`): 30 files, 542 tests passed.
- `@objectstack/runtime` local project, whole (four vitest shards): 384 files passed; 5777 tests passed, 19 skipped. `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` plus `check:test-typecheck`) exit 0.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` whole suite (three vitest shards): 236 files passed, 3 skipped; 28421 tests passed, 19 skipped. `typecheck` exit 0.
- `@objectstack/cli`, both tiers: unit 290 files, 4324 tests passed; integration 131 files passed; and CI's exact slice for `Test Core (2/6)` (`OS_TEST_SHARD=1/3`, both tiers): 141 files, 1956 tests passed, 1 skipped.

## Ablation (one-shot, not kept)

`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` reaches the pin through its `dist/`, so each leg rebuilt it and proved the marker's presence or absence there. At `addcca0cf5`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (WRAP mode; anchor 1 to 0, blob `04eee5b790` to `e70c5d7193`):

- mutate: the pre-flight's `if (others.length === 0 && !at.unbound) continue;` widened with a marker condition, so no row ever refuses; `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs`. Predicted 2 red / 3 green; observed 2 failed / 3 passed. Cases 1 and 2, on the re-seeded fixture, answered the card's defect: `400 PACKAGE_DELETE_PARTIAL`, `registryRemoved: true`, the shared object in `failed[]` with #23415's per-item `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` text, which is the same rows the pre-flight refuses.
- restore: blob equal to `HEAD` (`04eee5b7906ebe40733101d3f8815a5b5ececa30`), `git diff HEAD` empty, whole tree clean; rebuilt; `--absent` found the marker in none of 24 built files; the pin 5/5 green.

A first spelling of the mutation was refused by the tool (the replacement contained the anchor, so the anchor count could not drop) and restored at once; it measured nothing.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `addcca0cf5` derives 65 families. All 65 ran locally; `--ran` reconciles 65 derived, 65 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED. 63 exit 0. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, packages without `dist/`) and exited 0 once they were built. `check-empty-changeset.mjs --base origin/main` exits 1 on the 23415 note, the deliberate correction the maintainer confirmed (`6184266311`); CI's `Check Changeset` is red for the same reason, as on the previous head. Every other family CI runs is read from this PR's check-runs, not re-run here.

`Test Core (2/6)` (CLI slice 1/3) failed on `addcca0cf5` in CI run `38686154595`; the job log is not readable from the dev container. It did not reproduce: the slice passes locally, the whole CLI suite passes, the same shard was green on `7d36e8d205`, and the queue run on `5e97584201` (whose tree differs from `addcca0cf5` only in the runtime pin, which no CLI test reads) was green on `Test Core (2/6)`.

## Acceptance notes

- **#23415's unreleased changeset is corrected in one sentence**, the uninstall sentence of `.changeset/23415-drop-storage-other-rows.md`; the maintainer confirmed it on this PR (`6184266311`). `Check Changeset` stays red for it by design.
- **The per-item `409` stays as a safety net.** With the pre-flight, it is unreachable on the uninstall path except for a row written concurrently between the pre-flight and the per-item delete; then it is still caught and reported in `failed[]` as before.
- **Cost.** Without `keepData`, one `sys_metadata` read per active object row of the package (not `sys_`), the same read the per-item delete then repeats. With `keepData`, none.
- **File surface.** `protocol.ts`: the `deletePackage` docblock's step 3 and the pre-flight between step 3 and step 4 only. Not the per-item loop, `deleteMetaItem` or `classifyObjectContribution`.
- **The package-less row as the "other row".** A delete naming no package addresses the one package's row of an item while one is stored (`packagelessAddress`), so the package-less row cannot be deleted first through the metadata door while the package's row exists. The refusal's other way out (delete the package's own row first) covers that case; pinned as case 4's mechanism.
- **D9.9 gaps met while measuring, not fixed here: filed as #23630**, the D9.9 family close-out. Its two members:
  - a draft of a second package, saved before the owner's row and then promoted, stores an active row the registry cannot hold (measured above, at `publish-drafts` too);
  - the package-less-owner case that #23510 already noted.
- **A comment `main` left stale, not this PR's.** The `[#21276]` comment above step 3 in `deletePackage` still says the door answers that refusal "`500`, nothing changed". PR #23522 made it `409`. This PR does not edit that comment, because it lies outside this PR's change.
